why: Decides compatibility from the field table instead of the content hash, so a recipe differing only outside that table -- its title, budget, timeout, or any field added since the table was written -- is accepted as the same measuring instrument. The hash is what identifies the reviewed configuration; this is the plausible-looking implementation that silently compares against an unreviewed recipe.
killedBy: checkRecipeCompatibility still refuses when the hash differs but every compared field matches
